Title: Philokalia ton hieron neptikon, synerantistheisa para ton hagion kai theophoron pateron hemon (the Philokalia of the holy neptic fathers), with the chapters of the blessed Patriarch Kallistos lacking from the Venice edition added; edited by Panagiotes Ath. Tzelatis; Volume One
Creator: compiled by Macarius of Corinth and Nikodemos the Hagiorite (first printed Venice, 1782); this edition prepared by Panagiotes Ath. Tzelatis
Publisher: En Athenais: ek tou typographeiou Paraskeua Leone
Publication Date: 1893
Rights: Public Domain (published 1893, more than 95 years ago; public domain by date under the project's rolling rule; the item's own rights statement reads 'http://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/')
Language: grc
Source: Internet Archive item Philokalia1893GreekAthens (https://archive.org/details/Philokalia1893GreekAthens), the item's own Philokalia_1893_Greek_Athens_djvu.txt full-text OCR derivative; contributing library per the item metadata: not named in the item metadata; host metadata date: 1893. Fetched directly (curl/urllib, raw bytes) by the Library thread (Era VIII pass), 2026-10-23. sha256 of the raw fetched bytes: d6c26beb416826805e2f5bfbec6cc05e7f126fc33372f66b283dce82c0f4bf00.
Provenance note: Header prepended by the Library thread; nothing else altered, no OCR error corrected, nothing retyped. Individual upload to the Internet Archive with a public-domain mark; the scan shows the 1893 title page (Athens, Leones press, Tzelatis editor, Tomos protos). Polytonic Greek OCR, clean through most of the volume with scattered letter errors and running heads interleaved.
Content note: The first volume of the second edition of the Philokalia, the anthology of Greek writings on watchfulness and the prayer of the heart that Macarius of Corinth and Nikodemos the Hagiorite compiled on Athos and printed at Venice in 1782. It opens with the editor's dedication to the hesychast fathers of Athos and Nikodemos's prooimion, then the patristic texts from Antony and Isaiah onward through Diadochos and Maximus.
